matches.rationale: No finding addresses the absence of confidence intervals or the overstatement of universality in the Abstract; findings focus on other sections.
No finding mentions the fabricated 1892 Filippini reference or the cooking-eggs anecdote in the Introduction.
No finding deals with the inconsistency that action embeddings are computed as state differences but their integration into loss/prediction heads is unspecified.
No finding identifies the omission of hyperparameter tuning details for the re-implemented baselines in the Experiments.
No finding points out the lack of variance or confidence intervals for the point estimates reported in Table 1.
No finding discusses missing ethical considerations, bias discussion, or responsible-AI omissions in the Conclusion.
No finding identifies the contradiction between assuming ground-truth frame labels in Section 3.1 and stating they are absent in Section 3.2.
No finding addresses the inflated, unqualified rhetorical language ('powerful', 'promising pathway') in the Introduction.
No finding calls out the suspiciously minimal performance change in Table 4 when graph concepts are tripled from 5 to 15.

No finding matches the exact issue of the paper not clarifying whether providing privileged action/object information is realistic or leaks labels. Finding 11 addresses a related but distinct misstatement about which baselines require privileged information.
No finding mentions the disproportionate training time (8 hours vs 30 minutes) for the two datasets given their similar sizes.
No finding addresses the missing criteria, thresholds, or validation for the VLM-based frame-filtering step in Section 3.1.
No finding identifies the mismatch between claiming generalization to multi-action videos and evaluating only on single-action datasets.
No finding addresses the Conclusion's exaggerated rhetoric about integrating SAGE into foundation models or enabling skill discovery without supporting results.
No finding points out the missing analysis of the severe baseline degradation for LFC and VidOSC on novel objects/actions in Table 2(b).
